corpus.title: LatticeDB Embedded Property-Graph Architecture
corpus.text: LatticeDB is a serverless, embedded property-graph database designed for high-performance in-process execution. Operating similarly to SQLite for graph and vector data, LatticeDB eliminates remote database network boundaries by running entirely inside the host application process. It uniquely unites Cypher multi-hop graph queries with native HNSW vector similarity search using the <=> operator and BM25 inverted index text searches using the @@ operator in a single local binary file. Nodes follow a hierarchical schema comprising Document, Chunk, and Entity labels. Edges include [:HAS_CHUNK] linking documents to chunks, [:CONTAINS] linking chunks to extracted entities, and [:RELATION {type: ...}] linking entities together for multi-hop graph traversals. Because all indices share the same transactional storage layer, hybrid vector-graph queries execute with sub-millisecond latency.

corpus.title: FastEmbed Quantized Embeddings and Cross-Encoder Reranking
corpus.text: FastEmbed provides CPU-quantized dense and sparse vector generation without requiring GPU hardware. The default dense model is BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, generating 384-dimensional normalized vector embeddings optimized for cosine similarity. For precision stage-3 reranking, the engine integrates BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 in an INT8 quantized ONNX format from onnx-community/bge-reranker-v2-m3-ONNX. This cross-encoder features an 8,192 token context window, 568 million parameters, and executes inference in under 100 milliseconds on CPU via dynamic token batch padding. During reranking, graph paths traversed in LatticeDB are linearized into structured triples formatted as 'Entity1 --[RELATION]--> Entity2' and appended to candidate text chunks, allowing the cross-encoder to jointly score semantic text relevance and relational graph context.

corpus.title: GLiNER Zero-Shot Named Entity Recognition and Triples
corpus.text: The knowledge extraction pipeline employs GLiNER (Generalist and Lightweight Model for Named Entity Recognition). By default, the system leverages urchade/gliner_small-v2.1 as an efficient in-process extractor. GLiNER extracts domain entities corresponding to predefined labels including person, organization, technology, concept, algorithm, database, and protocol. Following entity extraction, the EntityExtractor extracts relation triples using sentence-level co-occurrence heuristics: when two entities co-occur within the same sentence, a semantic directed relationship edge [:RELATION] is created between their respective nodes in LatticeDB with relationship type derived from context. Extracted entities are tied to their originating text chunk through [:CONTAINS] edges, ensuring tight provenance tracking and citation grounding.

corpus.title: TypeSafe AI Jev System One Decision Architecture
corpus.text: TypeSafe AI Jev is a specialized System One decision model trained to provide fast, calibrated judgments rather than generating free-form conversational text. The pipeline utilizes three primary Jev primitives. First, the Choice primitive acts as a front-door router, classifying incoming prompts in 70 to 500 milliseconds into vector_exact, graph_relational, hybrid, chitchat, or massive_context routes. Second, the boolean Noul primitive serves as a context guardrail, evaluating retrieved candidate chunks in parallel and pruning tangential passages with relevance probability below 0.50. Third, the Score primitive evaluates content across ordered descriptive criteria, returning expected-value continuous scores and probability distributions. By decomposing complex workflows into small typed judgments, Jev ensures deterministic control, low token usage, and sub-second pipeline throughput.

corpus.title: Litestar and Granian Rust-Optimized Web Framework
corpus.text: The web API layer is built on Litestar 2.24+ and served by Granian, a high-performance HTTP server written in Rust that delivers 2 to 4 times the throughput of standard Python Uvicorn servers. All data transfer objects are defined as msgspec.Struct instances with rename='camel' to ensure zero-copy sub-millisecond JSON serialization. The service provides dual query APIs: a synchronous POST /api/v1/query endpoint and a streaming POST /api/v1/query/stream endpoint emitting typed Server-Sent Events (SSE) with stage, token, and done events for frontend telemetry. Error handling complies with RFC 9457 Problem Details, and all logging and error responses pass through automated regex sanitizers to scrub API keys, tokens, and authorization headers before reaching the network.

queries.query: Explain the multi-hop connection between an ingested Document and the relational entities extracted from it.
gold_chunks: Nodes follow a hierarchical schema comprising Document, Chunk, and Entity labels. Edges include [:HAS_CHUNK] linking documents to chunks, [:CONTAINS] linking chunks to extracted entities, and [:RELATION {type: ...}] linking entities together for multi-hop graph traversals.
queries.ground_truth: An ingested Document is linked to one or more Chunk nodes via [:HAS_CHUNK] edges. Each Chunk node is linked to the Entity nodes mentioned in its text via [:CONTAINS] edges. Those Entity nodes are then connected to other Entity nodes via [:RELATION] edges.

queries.query: How does the architecture prevent heavy CPU tasks like ONNX embeddings from blocking Litestar's async loop?
gold_chunks: To prevent the single-threaded asynchronous event loop from freezing, all CPU-bound machine learning tasks (embeddings, graph extraction) are strictly isolated in a ProcessPoolExecutor.
queries.ground_truth: All heavy CPU-bound machine learning tasks (embeddings, cross-encoder reranking, and entity extraction) are isolated in a dedicated ProcessPoolExecutor using run_in_pool(), offloading execution from Litestar's event loop.

queries.query: How does LatticeDB's in-process model compare with remote database architectures like Neo4j or Pinecone?

queries.ground_truth: LatticeDB operates as an embedded in-process database (like SQLite), eliminating the HTTP network latency (30-100ms) and heavy server infrastructure costs associated with remote databases like Neo4j or Pinecone.

queries.query: Describe the full end-to-end flow from receiving a user query to generating an SSE-streamed response.
gold_chunks: The web API layer is built on Litestar 2.24+ and served by Granian...
The Choice primitive acts as a front-door router...
LatticeDB uniquely unites Cypher multi-hop graph queries with native HNSW vector similarity search...
The boolean Noul primitive serves as a context guardrail...
emitting typed Server-Sent Events (SSE) with stage, token, and done events...
queries.ground_truth: The query arrives at Litestar (served by Granian). TypeSafe Jev Choice classifies the route while Tier 1 semantic cache is checked. On cache miss, Stage 1 hybrid search (HNSW + BM25 via RRF) recalls chunks from LatticeDB; Stage 2 traverses graph edges from entity anchors; Stage 3 reranks via bge-reranker-v2-m3 INT8 ONNX with linearized triples; Jev Noul prunes irrelevant chunks (threshold 0.50); GroqCloud qwen/qwen3.8-27b streams grounded answer tokens under a pybreaker circuit breaker; and Litestar emits typed SSE events (stage, token, done).
